steps.description: User login to obtain session ID for subsequent operations
steps.guidance: Call /v1/cl/user/login using POST method with required parameters including a timestamp and login body. The timestamp should be a Unix timestamp that is valid within 10 minutes.

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, expired in 10 minutes, type is int

input.name: body
input.description: Login request body containing username and password

output.name: response
output.description: Response object containing session_id and other information

steps.description: Create a DDoS attack flow template for simulating UDP flood attacks
steps.guidance: The purpose of this step is to create a DDoS attack flow template specifically for simulating UDP flood attacks. To do so, call the /v1/cl/ddos/attack/flow/create endpoint using POST method. Ensure that the timestamp parameter is a Unix timestamp valid within the next 10 minutes and provide a session_id obtained from a previous login or session creation API. The body should contain the necessary details as per the AttackFlowCreateRequest schema.

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, must be valid within the next 10 minutes

input.name: SESSION_ID
input.description: Allocated session id, obtained from a prior successful login or session creation

input.name: body
input.description: Details of the DDoS attack flow template to be created, as per the AttackFlowCreateRequest schema

output.name: response
output.description: Response containing the result of the DDoS attack flow template creation, as per the AttackFlowCreateResponse schema

steps.guidance: Call /v1/cl/ddos/attack/flow/param/update to update the DDoS attack flow parameters, including setting the traffic peak to 500Mbps, test duration to 60 seconds, and destination IP to 11.0.0.1/24. The timestamp should be a Unix timestamp valid for 10 minutes, and a session ID is required.

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, expired in 10 minutes, type is int

input.name: SESSION_ID
input.description: Allocated session id

input.name: body
input.description: Request body containing the updated DDoS attack flow parameters

output.name: response_body
output.description: Response body containing the result of the update operation

steps.description: 保存已配置好的DDoS攻击流量模板以便后续使用
steps.guidance: 通过POST方法调用/v1/cl/ddos/attack/flow/save接口，来保存一个已经配置完成的DDoS攻击流量模板。此请求需要在URL中包含一个有效期内（10分钟）的时间戳和会话ID，并且请求体中携带AttackFlowSaveRequest对象。

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, expired in 10 minutes, type is int

input.name: SESSION_ID
input.description: Allocated session id

input.name: body
input.description: AttackFlowSaveRequest object containing the DDoS attack flow template to be saved

output.name: response_body
output.description: The response body contains AttackFlowSaveResponse as defined in the API specification.

steps.description: Run a specified testcase with given ID
steps.guidance: This step aims to run a specific testcase using its ID. Call the /v1/cl/testcase/run endpoint via POST method. Ensure that you provide a valid session_id and timestamp (valid for 10 minutes) as query parameters, and include the necessary request body.

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: SESSION_ID
input.description: Allocated session id

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, expired in 10 minutes, type is int

input.name: body
input.description: Request body for running a testcase

steps.description: Search real-time category statistics for a specific test case instance
steps.guidance: Call /v1/cl/stats/category/search to retrieve various types of statistical information that can be collected during this test. This API requires a valid session_id and timestamp, where the timestamp should be a Unix timestamp and is valid for 10 minutes.

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, expired in 10 minutes, type is int

input.name: SESSION_ID
input.description: Allocated session id

input.name: body
input.description: Request body containing the details for the stats category search request

output.name: response_body
output.description: Response body containing the results of the stats category search

steps.description: Search statistics history of a specified testcase instance
steps.guidance: Call /v1/cl/stats/search using POST method to retrieve the historical statistical data. This API requires an unexpired timestamp and a valid session id, which should be obtained from previous steps.

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, expired in 10 minutes, type is int

input.name: SESSION_ID
input.description: Allocated session id

input.name: body
input.description: Request body for stats search, conforming to StatsSearchRequest schema

output.name: response
output.description: Response object containing the searched statistics, conforming to StatsSearchResponse schema

steps.guidance: Call /v1/cl/user/logout to safely log out the current user after completing all test steps. This requires a valid session_id and a timestamp that is not older than 10 minutes. The body of the request should follow the alps.UserLogoutRequest schema.

input.name: BASE_URL
input.description: API base without trailing slash

input.name: TIMESTAMP
input.description: Unix timestamp, expired in 10 minutes, type is int

input.name: SESSION_ID
input.description: Allocated session id

input.name: body
input.description: request body following the alps.UserLogoutRequest schema

output.name: response_body
output.description: response body following the alps.UserLogoutResponse schema
